topic_name: Political Regimes and Models of Democracy

166.question: The main criterion for distinguishing totalitarian from authoritarian regimes is...

options.A: The presence of a head of state
options.B: The existence of an apparatus of coercion
options.C: The degree to which the authorities claim control over social life
options.D: The use of a managerial hierarchy
options.E: The issuing of generally binding decisions

167.question: The information sphere of totalitarianism is characterized by...

options.A: Complete independence of the press combined with a ban on elections
options.B: The monopolization of information and the suppression of dissent
options.C: The state's neutrality toward all political doctrines
options.D: The mandatory absence of any means of mass communication
options.E: Competition among independent sources within a common legal framework

168.question: The organizational core of a totalitarian political system is...

options.A: Competition among several government coalitions
options.B: An independent board of arbitration judges
options.C: A centralized party fused with the state
options.D: An autonomous network of independent trade unions
options.E: A direct assembly of all citizens

169.question: Regarding force under authoritarianism, it is true that...

options.A: The regime may rely on the threat of force without constant mass repression
options.B: The regime excludes coercive resources from governance
options.C: Violence is possible only under universal suffrage
options.D: The security forces stand outside political leadership
options.E: The use of force necessarily extends to all spheres of life

170.question: Real political competition is banned, but private business and limited cultural pluralism are preserved. This corresponds most closely to...

options.A: Direct democracy
options.B: An authoritarian regime
options.C: A totalitarian regime
options.D: Liberal parliamentarism
options.E: Polyarchal democracy

171.question: Why is the mere existence of elections not enough to regard a regime as democratic?

options.A: Democracy requires only the appointment of leaders
options.B: Any elections exclude popular sovereignty
options.C: Electivity is characteristic only of totalitarianism
options.D: Elections can be held without real competition
options.E: Elections have no bearing on access to power

172.question: Co-optation of the political elite means...

options.A: The distribution of posts by lot
options.B: The hereditary transfer of every mandate to a successor
options.C: The dissolution of all governing bodies
options.D: The inclusion of new members by decision of the existing leading circle
options.E: The election of the entire apparatus in competitive elections

173.question: The concept of polyarchy for analyzing actually existing democracies was developed by...

options.A: Karl Deutsch
options.B: Robert Michels
options.C: Robert Dahl
options.D: Gaetano Mosca
options.E: Joseph Schumpeter

174.question: Distinguishing democracy as an ideal from polyarchy makes it possible to...

options.A: Prove the impossibility of any democratic institutions
options.B: Equate any regime with a parliament to a democracy
options.C: Exclude elections from the analysis of political systems
options.D: Reduce democracy to the personal virtue of a leader
options.E: Separate the normative image of popular rule from the empirical organization of competition

175.question: The minimal characteristics of democratic government:

options.A: Legal recognition of popular sovereignty
options.B: Periodic election of the main bodies
options.C: Subordination of political competition to a mandatory single doctrine
options.D: Reservation of leading posts to one irremovable group
options.E: Equality of citizens' political rights

176.question: The liberal-democratic model is characterized by...

options.A: Undivided power, estate status, inheritance
options.B: An organic whole, an imperative mandate, unity of interests
options.C: Unity of the general will, primacy of the common good, direct democracy
options.D: An official ideology, mobilization, a party monopoly
options.E: Sovereignty of the individual, representation, protection of the minority

177.question: In a comparative typology, the radical-democratic model is characterized by...

options.A: Political passivity and the autonomy of the economy
options.B: Separation of powers and the primacy of private interests
options.C: Hereditary legitimacy and estate representation
options.D: Sovereignty of the individual and a free parliamentary mandate
options.E: Sovereignty of the people and the direct exercise of power

178.question: An imperative mandate differs from a free one in that...

options.A: The deputy is appointed by the executive
options.B: Voters are forbidden to oversee the representative
options.C: The deputy is independent of any instructions
options.D: The deputy is bound by the binding instructions of the voters
options.E: The deputy's status is held for life

options.A: The transfer of decisions exclusively to professional deputies
options.B: The direct participation of citizens in decision-making
options.C: The hereditary transfer of supreme power
options.D: The election of intermediaries who then elect the head of state
options.E: The selection of leaders by judicial bodies alone

180.question: A referendum as a form of political participation differs from the election of deputies in that citizens...

options.A: Express an opinion only through a consultative poll
options.B: Vote directly on an issue rather than on the composition of representatives
options.C: Delegate the right to vote to party leaders
options.D: Give up their own participation in the decision
options.E: Necessarily approve the government's list of appointments

181.question: Indicate the correct correspondences between a model and a principle.

options.A: Liberal democracy: the primacy of the common good over individual autonomy
options.B: Radical democracy: an imperative mandate
options.C: Radical democracy: representation as the final transfer of sovereignty to deputies
options.D: Liberal democracy: unity of interests as the starting principle of society
options.E: Liberal democracy: a free mandate

182.question: Conditions that limit the transformation of majority rule into arbitrariness:

options.A: Legal limits on decision-making
options.B: Equality of political rights
options.C: Recognition of a majority decision as a sufficient ground for restricting any rights
options.D: Granting the ruling group the exclusive right to interpret the limits of its power
options.E: Protection of minority rights

183.question: Which comparisons of regimes are well founded?

options.A: The existence of elected institutions is a sufficient criterion of competitiveness
options.B: The preservation of a private economy means that rulers are accountable to the population
options.C: Authoritarianism allows the autonomy of certain non-political spheres
options.D: Totalitarianism strives for all-encompassing ideologization
options.E: Democracy presupposes the possibility of changing the leadership through elections

184.question: Only one pre-approved list is allowed in the elections, and independent associations are banned. Which conclusion is correct?

options.A: A single list means direct democracy
options.B: The mere fact of voting guarantees polyarchy
options.C: The appointment of candidates replaces popular sovereignty
options.D: An electoral procedure does not ensure political competition
options.E: The ban on associations ensures equality of opportunity

185.question: Which research conclusion requires distinguishing the normative from the empirical understanding of democracy?

options.A: The authorities' declarations of the goals of government are equivalent to observing real competition
options.B: The study of institutions makes it possible to disregard the actual availability of political rights
options.C: A declaration of popular rule does not prove that real institutions meet democratic criteria
options.D: The procedural formalization of power makes checking the turnover of leadership redundant
options.E: The lack of a complete match with the ideal deprives empirical criteria of significance
